title: Failed Search Profile writes leave changed profiles active until reload
owner: B profile persistence; I recovery; J feedback
repro: Inject targeted localStorage setItem QuotaExceededError or SecurityError on bamendjou:search-profiles. Through Step 3 save, update, rename and delete the synthetic baseline profile. All four operations change the real in-memory store although exact saved bytes remain unchanged. Applying the failed update reads Bearish while saved baseline remains Bullish; reload restores the old data. Eight cases reproduce this. No saved bytes were corrupted in these cases.
expected: Keep committed profiles aligned with readback, or present an explicit unsaved/error state that cannot masquerade as a saved profile.
retest: Both exception types across CRUD; verify raw bytes, rendered profiles, effective apply behavior, reload and successful retry.

title: Theme changes do not synchronize across tabs as Settings promises
repro: Open two same-origin Settings tabs, change light to dark in one. The other receives a native storage event and can read dark from localStorage, but remains light. The Theme row explicitly promises "Persisted in localStorage; synced across tabs" at page.tsx:225. Browser-process restart correctly restores dark.
expected: The other tab updates its theme after the storage change; reconcile the explicit UI promise with supported behavior.
retest: Both directions in two tabs, saved readback, same-tab application and process restart. This is a UI defect below the numeric gate.

title: An ordinary Settings edit in a stale tab overwrites unrelated saved values
repro: Use normal Settings UI to set Markov lookback35; open a second same-origin tab. In tab A set lookback55. In stale tab B change confidence caution to64 and blur. The whole-store write silently changes saved lookback55 back to35. This case uses no importer, direct harness storage writes or injected failure; exact raw bytes and storage events are captured.
expected: An edit to confidence preserves the newer saved Markov value or surfaces a conflict. A normal two-tab edit must not silently lose unrelated persisted data.
retest: Different-field and same-field stale-tab edits, raw bytes/reload, explicit conflict/recovery behavior; preserve storage keys and schema compatibility.

title: Saving after invalid scan schedule YAML overwrites the only recovery bytes
owner: B schedule persistence; I recovery; G scheduled consumers
repro: In a temporary actual ScanScheduleStore, load malformed syntax (entries: [unterminated), a wrong root list, or an invalid version string. Each silently yields an empty list while initially preserving the file. Upsert a real-schema-valid captured options entry. The next ordinary write replaces the original file with version2 data and creates no backup. Three variants reproduce one recovery loss mechanism; no real configuration was used.
expected: An unresolved load failure blocks ordinary mutation or preserves the original bytes for recovery and exposes the failure.
retest: Each invalid-load variant followed by normal API create/update; exact original backup or refusal, surfaced error and independent process reopening. Existing #374 concerns four other schedule stores and failed-write memory rollback, a different mechanism.

title: Scheduled scan failures and unresolvable profile selections give no explanation
owner: B Settings schedule UI; G automation; J presentation
evidence: settings-states/output.json schedule-invalid-cadence-feedback, schedule-update-failure-feedback, schedule-delete-failure-feedback, schedule-legacy-profile-refusal; settings-states/findings.md items3/5
repro: With explicit mocked responses, cadence0 gets schema-equivalent422 and silently snaps back to35; label blur500 leaves Failed draft displayed while the ledger retains Renamed fixed; delete500 leaves the row without an error. Selecting a synthetic legacy options profile missing required fields throws in the actual resolver; no PUT occurs and the prior request is preserved, but no explanation appears. Successful operations/readbacks pass.
expected: Explain the failed operation or unresolvable profile, identify any unsaved draft and permit a clear retry. Keep the prior committed record.
retest: All three HTTP failures and resolver failure followed by successful retry/remount; verify no false success or mutation. These are UI feedback defects; mocks do not prove a real backend write failure.

title: A schedule with a missing profile visually selects a different saved profile
owner: B profile/schedule presentation; G consumer; J UI
repro: Mount a synthetic schedule whose saved profile_id is deleted-profile while available options contain only audit-options-b. The controlled select retains the missing value but Chromium renders Audit options B as selected. The saved id and resolved request are unchanged. No automatic mutation is inferred.
expected: Display an explicit unavailable/missing profile option with its stored identity until the operator deliberately reassigns it.
retest: Delete a referenced profile, remount Settings, verify displayed identity and saved snapshot; explicitly choose another profile and verify request/readback.

title: An unavailable timezone readback displays an editable default without an error
owner: B Settings readback; G/H/D scheduler consumers; J feedback
repro: Initial GET /settings/scheduling returns mocked503 while the fixture stored timezone is Asia/Tokyo. The field displays its initial Europe/Berlin default with no loading/error/unknown marker. This is the failed initial-load path, distinct from #372 late successful GET overwriting an edit. Scheduler timing was not executed.
expected: Distinguish unavailable readback from a confirmed stored timezone; an unconfirmed default must not look like the saved server value.
retest: Pending/failing/recovered initial GET, informed edits and saved readback. Coordinate with #372 and serial Settings changes; no claim that a scheduler used the displayed timezone.
